reason: All key premises are directly supported by the single cited study (E1, E2, E3), which reports the exact intervention, mechanism, and quantitative improvements in the same alloy class and temperature range. However, the evidence comes from only one paper on one SLM-processed HEA, so the generalizability premise to other precipitation-strengthened HEAs is an overstatement not yet supported by additional independent evidence.
premises: Slow cooling from solution treatment coarsens precipitates that interact with grain boundaries to create serrated morphology
Serrated grain boundaries reduce local strain concentrations and impede intergranular crack propagation
Serrated grain boundaries significantly improve tensile ductility (3–4×) and creep rupture life (up to 400×) at 650°C
The mechanism is demonstrated by molecular dynamics simulations showing more homogeneous strain distribution along serrated boundaries
The approach is applicable to precipitation-strengthened HEAs in the 600–700°C range
